title: Subject expansion: foundation practice across 12 core subjects
sourcePolicy: All questions are original subject-wise practice questions, not official PYQs. Explanations include the key concept and common distinctions; verify current legal and policy changes against the latest official text.

questions.q: A price is increased by 20% and then reduced by 20%. What is the net effect on the original price?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC LDA / Secretariat LDA
questions.source: Original arithmetic practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Worked solution checked independently; original practice, not an official PYQ.
questions.e: Let the original price be ₹100. After a 20% increase it becomes ₹120. A 20% reduction on ₹120 is ₹24, so the final price is ₹96. The net change is ₹4 below ₹100, or a 4% decrease. The two percentages do not cancel because the second percentage is calculated on the changed amount. Shortcut: for successive changes of +a% and −b%, net percentage change = a − b − ab/100; here 20 − 20 − 400/100 = −4%.

o: Each of the applicants have submitted the form.
Each of the applicants has submitted the form.
Each of the applicant have submitted the form.
Each applicants has submitted the form.
questions.source: Original English grammar practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Checked against standard subject–verb agreement rules; original practice, not an official PYQ.
questions.e: The correct sentence is “Each of the applicants has submitted the form.” The subject is the singular pronoun “each”, so it takes the singular verb “has”. The plural noun “applicants” appears in the prepositional phrase “of the applicants” and does not control the verb. “Have” would agree with a plural subject, not with “each”. In exam questions, identify the true subject before selecting the verb.

questions.q: Meghalaya became a full-fledged state of India on which date?
questions.source: Meghalaya statehood fact; original practice question
questions.verificationStatus: Date distinguishes the Autonomous State (1970) from full statehood (1972); original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Meghalaya attained full statehood on 21 January 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971. It had earlier become an autonomous State within Assam on 2 April 1970. These are two different constitutional milestones and should not be confused. The date 21 January is also observed as Meghalaya Statehood Day.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws?
questions.source: Constitution of India; original practice question
questions.verificationStatus: Article reference checked against the Constitution; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Article 12 defines “the State” for Part III. Article 19 protects specified freedoms, while Article 21 protects life and personal liberty. Remember the distinction: Article 14 is the general equality guarantee; Article 15 addresses specified grounds of discrimination.

questions.q: Which event is traditionally associated with Emperor Ashoka's change towards Dhamma and non-violence?
questions.source: Original ancient Indian history practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Standard historical account; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: The Kalinga War is associated with Ashoka's remorse over the suffering caused by conquest and his subsequent emphasis on Dhamma. His Major Rock Edict XIII refers to the Kalinga campaign and the human cost of war. The other battles belong to much later periods: Plassey (1757), Panipat (1761) and Haldighati (1576).

questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer concentrated?
questions.source: Original geography practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Standard atmospheric science fact; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, roughly 10–50 km above Earth's surface, with the greatest concentration commonly around 20–30 km. This ozone absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. The troposphere is the lowest layer where most weather occurs; the mesosphere lies above the stratosphere.

questions.q: Which component of blood is primarily responsible for transporting oxygen?
questions.source: Original general science practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Standard human physiology fact; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) transport most oxygen using haemoglobin, an iron-containing protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in tissues. White blood cells are mainly involved in defence, while platelets help blood clot. Plasma carries dissolved substances, including some carbon dioxide, nutrients and hormones.

questions.q: Which of the following is the clearest example of government capital expenditure?
o: Construction of a government hospital building
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / MPSC / DSC LDA
questions.source: Union Budget: Key to Budget Documents; original practice question
questions.verificationStatus: Distinction checked against the Union Budget explanatory document; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Construction of a government hospital building creates a durable asset and is therefore a typical example of capital expenditure. Salaries, electricity bills and routine rent are generally revenue expenditure because they meet recurring operating costs and do not themselves create a government asset. The Union Budget's explanatory document describes capital payments as including acquisition of assets such as land, buildings, machinery and equipment.

questions.q: The Environment (Protection) Act of India was enacted in which year?
questions.verificationStatus: Year checked against the official Act text on India Code; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: The Environment (Protection) Act is Act No. 29 of 1986. It was enacted to provide for the protection and improvement of the environment and matters connected with it. Do not confuse it with the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, or the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. The Act's long title and enactment date appear on the official India Code text.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, __.
questions.source: Original reasoning practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Pattern verified by first differences and square-number relation; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: The first differences are 5, 7, 9 and 11. They increase by 2 each time, so the next difference is 13. Therefore, 35 + 13 = 48. Another way to see the pattern is n² + 2n for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, giving 3, 8, 15, 24, 35; for n = 6 the value is 48. Always test the differences before guessing a series rule.

questions.q: Which statement best describes RAM in a computer?
o: It is permanent storage that retains data without power.
It is volatile working memory used by active programs.
It is the device that prints documents.
It is the computer's main input device.
questions.source: Original computer fundamentals practice; not official PYQ
questions.verificationStatus: Standard computer fundamentals definition; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile working memory. It temporarily holds data and instructions that the processor is actively using; its contents are normally lost when power is switched off. An SSD or hard disk provides non-volatile storage. A printer is an output device, while a keyboard and mouse are input devices.

questions.q: Under Section 16(1) of the CGST Act, input tax credit is generally available on eligible supplies used or intended to be used in which connection?
o: The course or furtherance of business
Any activity, whether business-related or not
Only the purchase of immovable property
questions.source: CGST Act, 2017, Section 16(1), official GST Council-hosted text
questions.verificationStatus: Core principle checked against Section 16(1); eligibility remains subject to statutory conditions and restrictions; original practice, not official PYQ.
questions.e: Section 16(1) provides that a registered person may be entitled to credit of input tax on supplies of goods or services or both used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business, subject to the Act's conditions and restrictions. This is not an unrestricted credit for personal consumption. A complete ITC examination must also consider Section 16(2), blocked credits under Section 17(5), prescribed rules and relevant facts.
